The best-fit model is the *truth*, not the data. It's a noise-free curve, so "regenerating" just means: synthetic = best_fit_model + fresh noise drawn from the real error bars, with the same masks and resolution. Then you fit that and ask whether you get the input parameters back.

Why not reuse the observation itself? Because its residuals are real noise plus whatever the model gets wrong, so you never know the true answer to compare against. Starting from the fit gives you a case where the model is exactly right and the truth is known, so any bias or scatter you see is purely the inference pipeline. Using several noise draws (fixed seeds, per `wiki/research/questions/q-mock-recovery.md`) turns one lucky or unlucky realisation into an actual scatter estimate.
